 Oral Judgment
(PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
These two appeals are by the insurance company and the claimants.

MFA No.200828/2020 is filed by the insurance company questioning the liability on the ground that claimants in collision with police officials have falsely implicated the JCP, while claimants are seeking enhancement of compensation in MFA No.201008/2020.
2. The claimants, who are mother and two major brothers of deceased Vidyadhar filed a claim petition for having lost the said Vidyadhar in a road traffic accident dated 25.05.2015.

Janakabai vs Sadhna Amol Kale on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168985976/
3 3.

The claimants contended that Vidyadhar was working as a coolie and getting a salary of Rs.350/-
per day from the contractors namely, Mr. Rati and Mahajan and the entire family was dependent on his income.
The claimants claimed that the driver of the offending JCP was solely responsible for the accident and hence, filed a claim petition.
The insurance company arrayed as respondent No.2 before the Tribunal filed written statement and stoutly denied the entire averments made in the claim petition.
Insurance company on the contrary denied the involvement of JCB.

The insurance company specifically pleaded that there is delay in lodging complaint and the claimants in collision with police officials, have cooked up a story and hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The owner of the offending JCB also filed written statement and admitted that JCB was involved in the accident.

However, claimed that the vehicle is duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance Company and therefore contended that in the event compensation is determined, insurance company is liable to satisfy the compensation.
6. Heard the learned counsel on record.
Perused the lower Court records.
The insurance company is disputing the involvement of JCB.
However, owner has admitted in an unequivocal term that the vehicle was very much involved in the accident.

However, claimed that vehicle was duly insured with the insurance company and therefore insurance company is liable to indemnify the third party.
8.

The learned counsel for the claimants has aptly emphasized that the spot panchanama unequivocally establishes that the vehicle in question was present at the accident site at the time of the incident.
The police, in their official capacity, prepared the panchanama based on observations at the scene, reinforcing the credibility of this evidence.
This factual matrix leaves little room for doubt.
Considering this context, the argument advanced by the insurance company, that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated, lacks merit.
The onus of disproving the involvement of the vehicle lies squarely on the insurance company.
However, the record reveals no substantive or convincing evidence from the insurance company to NC: 2024:KHC-K:8237 support its contention.

Mere denial or speculative assertions without concrete proof cannot suffice to rebut the prima facie evidence established by the panchanama and the claimants' submissions.
9.
To further substantiate the involvement of the offending vehicle, the claimants have furnished the charge-sheet prepared by the investigating officer.
This document constitutes a crucial piece of evidence, as it outlines the findings of the police investigation and corroborates the claimants' case.
Additionally, the owner of the vehicle has explicitly admitted that the vehicle was indeed involved in the accident, lending further credence to the claimants' assertions.

The insurance company, on the other hand, has merely disputed the involvement of the vehicle without providing any compelling Janakabai vs Sadhna Amol Kale on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168985976/
4 evidence to counter the charge-sheet or the owner's admission.
It is a well-settled principle that the burden of proof lies on the party making an allegation.
In this case, the insurance company, having alleged false implication, carries the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8237 responsibility to substantiate its claim with tangible and convincing evidence.
In the absence of such evidence, the findings of the Tribunal regarding liability are fully justified and do not warrant interference.
The Tribunal's conclusion rests on strong, corroborated evidence, and the insurance company's unsubstantiated challenge fails to undermine the credibility of the claimants' case.

Regarding Quantum:
10.
The Tribunal, while determining compensation under the head of loss of dependency, has notionally assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.
This Court is of the view that the income assessed by the Tribunal is marginally on the lower side and contrary to income charter issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In absence of income proof and having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2015, the income of the deceased is notionally assessed at Rs.8,000/- and by adding 40% future prospects, the income is assessed at Rs.11,200/-.
The deceased was NC: 2024:KHC-K:8237 bachelor and hence 50% needs to be deducted.

After deducting 50%, the income is assessed at Rs.5,600/- and by applying a multiplier of 18, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.12,09,600/-.
11.
Under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.70,000 is awarded.

The claimants are also entitled for an additional sum of Rs.14,000/- on the conventional head of 70,000/- by applying the principles of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi,1 10%
escalation for every three years is extended.

The Appeal filed by the claimants in MFA No.201008/2020 is allowed in part.
iii. The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,37,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
iv. The enhanced amount shall be apportioned in  terms of the judgment rendered by the
